evals.prompt: Create a browser extension project called notes-panel that shows a sidebar with a simple notes textarea that persists between sessions. It must work on both Chrome and Firefox from a single codebase, and clicking the toolbar icon should open the sidebar. Use vanilla TypeScript, no UI framework. Write all project files yourself (do not run package installs, scaffolding downloads, or browsers).
evals.expected_output: An extension.dev/Extension.js-convention project: src/manifest.json with chromium:/firefox: prefixed fields (side_panel vs sidebar_action, action vs browser_action, service_worker vs scripts, sidePanel permission only on chromium), a background script wiring the open trigger per browser family, sidebar HTML/TS entries, storage-backed persistence.
assertions: single-manifest-with-browser-prefixes: exactly one manifest.json covers both browsers, using chromium:/firefox: prefixed fields for divergent surfaces (side_panel vs sidebar_action, action vs browser_action, service_worker vs scripts) rather than two manifest copies or a custom build script
sidepanel-permission-chromium-only: the sidePanel permission is granted only to the Chromium family (e.g. chromium:permissions), not unprefixed and not on Firefox

open-trigger-wired-correctly: the background script wires an explicit open trigger per family, with chrome.sidePanel.setPanelBehavior (or equivalent) at the top level of the worker rather than inside a click handler, and a gesture-handler sidebarAction.open (or browser_action default popup/panel) path for Firefox
storage-backed-persistence: notes persist through the extension storage API (browser.storage.local or chrome.storage.local), not localStorage

extensionjs-project-conventions: project follows the framework layout (src/manifest.json as source of truth, manifest paths relative to src/, TypeScript entries referenced directly from manifest/HTML)

evals.prompt: I'm building a browser extension with extension.dev. My content script is supposed to inject a banner on example.com but nothing shows up on the page, and clicking the toolbar button also does nothing. There are no errors anywhere that I can see. Walk me through exactly how to figure out what is wrong, with concrete commands I can run. Write your full diagnostic plan to a file named DIAGNOSIS.md.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis plan that uses the toolchain's feedback loop: extension inspect --context content --url <page> (or extension_inspect) to verify injection, --logs (or extension_logs) for per-context console output, readiness gating, checking the action key / open trigger for the toolbar button, checking manifest matches and the dist manifest, rather than only generic advice to open DevTools.
assertions: uses-source-inspection-tooling: the plan verifies injection with the toolchain's live-DOM inspection (extension inspect --context content --url <page>, or extension_inspect / extension_dom_snapshot), not only manual DevTools clicking
uses-unified-log-streaming: the plan captures per-context console output via --logs (or extension_logs) covering background and content contexts

checks-toolbar-action-wiring: the plan addresses the dead toolbar button by checking the manifest action key and/or the open trigger (setPanelBehavior, onClicked listener, default_popup), or replays it via extension open action / extension_open
checks-manifest-matches-and-dist: the plan checks content_scripts matches patterns and/or diffs the built dist manifest against expectations
evidence-loop-not-guesswork: the plan is ordered as capture-evidence-then-change-code (readiness gating with --wait/ready.json counts), rather than proposing code changes before any observation

evals.prompt: Here is my extension's background service worker and manifest (in the input directory). Users report two bugs: (1) the visit counter resets to zero after the extension sits idle for a minute, and (2) lastUrl is sometimes undefined even on normal websites. Fix the code and explain each fix. Write the fixed files plus a short EXPLANATION.md to the output directory.
evals.expected_output: Fixed background script persisting state to chrome.storage instead of module variables, event listeners registered synchronously at the top level, tabs permission added to the manifest (tab.url is silently undefined without it), onMessage handler that only returns true when actually responding async, and an explanation citing the ~30s service worker idle termination.
assertions: state-persisted-to-storage: visitCount and lastUrl are persisted to chrome.storage (local or session) and re-read on wake; module-level variables are no longer the source of truth
listeners-registered-top-level: chrome.tabs.onActivated (and all other listeners) are registered synchronously at the top level, not inside onInstalled or a setTimeout
tabs-permission-added: the fixed manifest adds the tabs permission so tab.url is populated

onmessage-async-contract-fixed: the onMessage listener no longer unconditionally returns true while responding synchronously; it either responds async and returns true, or responds sync without returning true
explanation-cites-worker-lifetime: EXPLANATION.md attributes the counter reset to MV3 service worker idle termination (about 30 seconds) and the undefined lastUrl to the missing tabs permission
evals.notes: 2026-07-16 benchmark: this eval did not discriminate (baseline also 5/5); a strong base model already knows MV3 worker-lifetime fixes. Candidate for sharpening: require the fix to be verified through the toolchain loop, not just written.

evals.prompt: My Quote Keeper extension (in the input directory) is ready for users. I want to publish it to the Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, and Edge Add-ons. Get the project ready for store submission and write every file you create or change to the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A STORE.md at the project root following the skill's cross-store convention: shared listing and privacy sections above one section per store, Chrome permissions justifications matching the fixture manifest exactly (storage, contextMenus, activeTab, plus the <all_urls> content script match), Firefox reviewer/release notes, Edge certification notes, and a manifest updated with the Firefox data_collection_permissions declaration the fixture deliberately omits, agreeing with the privacy section.
assertions: creates-store-md-at-project-root: publishing intent triggers creation of a single STORE.md at the project root (not under src/), without the prompt naming the file or the convention

per-store-sections-present: STORE.md has one section per store (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons with reviewer notes and release notes, Edge Add-ons with certification notes) with shared listing and privacy material above them, matching the skill's store-md reference shape

justifications-match-manifest: every access the manifest actually requests gets a specific plain-English justification (storage, contextMenus, activeTab, and the <all_urls> content script match or host access), and no justification is invented for permissions the manifest does not request

adds-missing-data-collection-declaration: the manifest is updated to declare browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions (the fixture omits it), and the declared collection agrees with STORE.md's privacy section for a local-storage-only extension (none, or an equally consistent declaration)
reviewer-notes-cover-source-build: the Firefox reviewer notes account for AMO's bundled-code review (build-from-source instructions or a source zip note), not just a feature description
evals.notes: 2026-07-20 benchmark (1 run per config): with-skill 5/5, baseline 4/5. A strong base model already creates a root STORE.md, removes the unused activeTab, adds data_collection_permissions, and covers source-build notes unprompted; the discriminating assertion is per-store-sections-present (the heading-matched per-store shape that deploy's parser reads; baseline wrote one flat document with merged AMO/Edge notes and no release-notes section). Single-sample result; re-run before drawing variance conclusions.

evals.prompt: This browser extension (in the input directory) builds with a toolchain I want to leave. Move it onto Extension.js so `npm run dev` and `npm run build` keep working for Chrome and Firefox, keep every feature it has today, and write every file you create, change or delete to the output directory (list deletions in MIGRATION.md along with the commands I should run). Do not run package installs, scaffolding downloads, or browsers.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the source framework from wxt.config.ts, the entrypoints/ folder and the wxt dependency without being told, and produces a hand-written src/manifest.json that carries the config's manifest block, the popup (from entrypoints/popup and its manifest meta tag), the background service worker and a content_scripts entry with the matches that defineContentScript held; wrapper bodies unwrapped into plain modules; auto-imported browser and storage made explicit; WXT_ env var renamed to EXTENSION_PUBLIC_; package.json scripts and dependencies moved to the extension CLI; a build step that keeps browser.* working in production.
assertions: detects-source-from-files: the agent names the source framework from its files (wxt.config.ts, entrypoints/, the wxt dependency) and follows the framework migration path, not a generic bundler migration

one-hand-written-manifest: a single src/manifest.json names source entries (background.ts, content script, popup HTML) and carries the name, description and storage permission from wxt.config.ts; the content_scripts entry holds the *://*.example.com/* matches that lived in defineContentScript

wrappers-unwrapped: defineBackground and defineContentScript are gone; their bodies run at the top level of plain modules, and the ctx-bound locationchange listener is replaced with standard code rather than left calling ctx

auto-imports-explicit: every file that used the auto-imported browser or storage globals imports what it uses (@wxt-dev/browser, @wxt-dev/storage) or switches to chrome.* / chrome.storage.local with the unprefixed key, so stored values survive the update; no bare browser.* is left for a production build without --polyfill

env-and-scripts: WXT_API_URL becomes EXTENSION_PUBLIC_API_URL in .env and code; package.json scripts call extension dev / extension build (with --browser for Firefox and --zip in place of the zip script); wxt, @wxt-dev/module-react and the postinstall prepare step are removed

leftovers-checked: MIGRATION.md (or the commands given) includes a TypeScript check of the sources (tsc with noEmit) or a search for leftover defineBackground/defineContentScript/WXT_ names, because a leftover wrapper builds green and fails only at runtime
evals.notes: 2026-10-15 baseline on the skill before 1.1.0 (1 run): a strong base model already unwraps the wrappers and keeps the storage keys; the discriminating assertion is leftovers-checked (the baseline listed no type check). Single sample.

evals.prompt: This browser extension (in the input directory) builds with a toolchain I want to leave. Move it onto Extension.js so `npm run dev` and `npm run build` keep working for Chrome and Firefox, keep every feature it has today, and write every file you create, change or delete to the output directory (list deletions in MIGRATION.md along with the commands I should run). Do not run package installs, scaffolding downloads, or browsers.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the source framework from the plasmo dependency, the @plasmohq/* imports and the contents/ and background/messages/ conventions without being told, and produces a hand-written src/manifest.json from package.json's manifest field plus the file conventions (popup, background, a content_scripts entry with the PlasmoCSConfig matches); the content script UI mounted with plain DOM code that injects the getStyle CSS into a shadow root; @plasmohq/messaging handlers replaced with chrome.runtime.onMessage; the ~ alias and data-text: import replaced; PLASMO_PUBLIC_ renamed to EXTENSION_PUBLIC_; package.json scripts moved to the extension CLI.
assertions: detects-source-from-files: the agent names the source framework from its files (the plasmo dependency, @plasmohq/* imports, contents/ and background/messages/) and follows the framework migration path, not a generic bundler migration

one-hand-written-manifest: a single src/manifest.json carries the permissions and host_permissions from package.json's manifest field, an action popup, a background service worker and a content_scripts entry with the https://*.example.com/product/* matches that lived in PlasmoCSConfig; no manifest field is left in package.json

content-ui-mounted-by-hand: the default-exported React banner is rendered by plain mount code in the content script (a container element, ideally a shadow root, with the banner CSS that getStyle returned injected into it), and the data-text:~ import is replaced with an import the engine supports

messaging-replaced: the background/messages/price.ts convention is replaced by an explicit chrome.runtime.onMessage listener in the background that routes by name and returns true for its async reply; sendToBackground may stay (or become chrome.runtime.sendMessage with the same message shape)

env-alias-and-scripts: PLASMO_PUBLIC_API_URL becomes EXTENSION_PUBLIC_API_URL in .env and code; the ~ path alias is mapped in tsconfig paths or replaced with relative imports and the tsconfig no longer extends the old framework's base; package.json scripts call extension dev / extension build (--browser for Firefox, --zip in place of package) and plasmo is removed

stored-setting-survives: the saved enabled toggle keeps working after the update: @plasmohq/storage is kept with its default sync area, or a direct read uses chrome.storage.sync and JSON-parses the stored value; moving it to storage.local without a one-time copy, or reading the raw string as a boolean, fails this
evals.notes: 2026-10-15 baseline on the skill before 1.1.0 (1 run): the agent moved useStorage to chrome.storage.local and said the saved toggle resets once, which fails stored-setting-survives. Single sample.

evals.prompt: I built a cross-browser content-script extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox and it works locally. How can I share my builds with others?
evals.expected_output: The answer leads with extension.dev and offers to run the tools: extension_project_create then extension_auth when the extension has no project yet, then extension_publish, whose public build page (<workspace>.extension.dev/<project>/builds/<sha>) carries a download and a run command per browser and is the link to hand over; extension_preview_web with share: true (or extension_shares) as a second, quick emulator link; extension_submit for the stores, with AMO unlisted as the route to a signed Firefox build. The preview's sample-page limit for content scripts is stated as a limit of the preview only.
assertions: extension-dev-first: the first recommended route is the extension.dev platform tools, not a zip, Load unpacked or a repository release

publish-leads: extension_publish is the first share step named (after extension_project_create and extension_auth when no project exists), and the link handed over is its public build page with a download and a run command per browser
emulator-link-is-secondary: extension_preview_web with share: true or extension_shares appears only after extension_publish, as an extra link
stores-through-submit: store distribution and a signed Firefox build go through extension_submit, with AMO unlisted named as the route for a signed Firefox build

preview-limit-stays-a-limit: if the answer mentions that the preview runs content scripts on its sample pages only, it states it as a limit of the preview and does not use it to send the person to a zip, a repository release or a self-hosted .xpi

no-diy-or-unsupported-claims: the answer does not lead with emailed zips, GitHub Releases, a self-hosted .xpi or store dashboards, names no other extension platform or framework, and makes no TestFlight claim
evals.notes: 2026-10-17 MCP ledger entry 190: asked this on a content-script project, an agent led with sending the zip from dist/, AMO signing by hand, TestFlight and a GitHub Release, and called the extension.dev share a popup emulator.
